mcqs.question: Consider the statements p: "It is raining" and q: "I carry an umbrella". Construct the truth table for the compound statement (p ∧ q) → ¬p. What is the truth value of the statement when p = True and q = False?
mcqs.explanation: When p = True and q = False, p ∧ q = False. ¬p = False. An implication (False → False) is always true. Hence the compound statement evaluates to True. Options B, C, D are incorrect because the implication rule makes the statement true in this case.

mcqs.question: Let p denote "n is even" and q denote "n > 10". Which compound statement correctly expresses "n is even and greater than 10"?
mcqs.explanation: The word "and" corresponds to the logical conjunction, denoted by ∧. Therefore the correct representation is p ∧ q. Option A is disjunction, C is implication, and D negates p, so they do not match the required meaning.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about the logical disjunction p ∨ q is incorrect?

options.A: It is true when at least one of p or q is true.
options.B: It is false only when both p and q are false.
options.C: It is true only when both p and q are true.
options.D: It is true when p is true and q is false.

mcqs.answer: It is true only when both p and q are true.
mcqs.explanation: A disjunction is true if at least one operand is true; it is false only when both are false. Hence statement C, which says it is true only when both are true, is the misconception. Options A, B, and D correctly describe the truth conditions of p ∨ q.

mcqs.question: For statements p and q, the implication p → q is false only in which case?

options.A: p is true and q is false
options.B: p is false and q is true
options.C: Both p and q are true
options.D: Both p and q are false

mcqs.answer: p is true and q is false
mcqs.explanation: An implication is false only when the antecedent (p) is true while the consequent (q) is false. In all other combinations the implication is true. Therefore option A is the only case that makes p → q false.

mcqs.question: Which of the following best describes the truth condition of the biconditional statement p ↔ q?

options.A: True when p and q have the same truth value, false otherwise
options.B: True only when both p and q are true
options.C: True only when p is true and q is false
options.D: True when at least one of p or q is true

mcqs.answer: True when p and q have the same truth value, false otherwise
mcqs.explanation: A biconditional p ↔ q is true exactly when both statements share the same truth value—both true or both false. Options B, C, and D describe other connectives (conjunction, a specific false case, and disjunction) and are therefore incorrect.

mcqs.question: Consider the compound statement (p ∨ q) → (p ∧ r). For the row where p = False, q = True, and r = False, what is the truth value of the whole statement?
mcqs.explanation: First compute p ∨ q = False ∨ True = True. Next compute p ∧ r = False ∧ False = False. The implication True → False is false. Hence the compound statement evaluates to False. Options A, C, and D are incorrect based on the implication rule.

mcqs.question: In logical connectives, the conjunction of two statements p and q, denoted p ∧ q, is true exactly when:

options.A: Both p and q are true
options.B: At least one of p or q is true
options.C: p is true and q is false
options.D: Both p and q are false

mcqs.answer: Both p and q are true
mcqs.explanation: Conjunction (AND) requires both component statements to be true for the whole expression to be true. All other options describe different truth conditions.

mcqs.question: The logical disjunction p ∨ q is false only when:

options.A: Both p and q are false
options.B: At least one of p or q is true
options.C: Both p and q are true
options.D: p is true and q is false

mcqs.answer: Both p and q are false
mcqs.explanation: A disjunction (OR) yields false only in the case where both operands are false. In every other combination it is true. Hence option A correctly states the condition.
